commenti.body: Which version of  Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory is better, the Tim Burton version or the Gene Wilder version?

It depends on what you're looking for and what you consider makes a film better. The original is a classic, Gene Wilder gives an amazing performance, and it has some songs that really stick in one's head. That being said, it does struggle with pacing at times, most notably with Cheer Up Charlie, has some odd plot changes from the book e.g. Slugworth is a double agent, and has some tone issues with some of its comedy and of course the fever dream of a blast ride.

The 2005 movie is generally a more faithful adaptation of the book and Johnny Depp also gives a decent performance. The movie definitely has the look and feel of Burton though and for some this is either a positive or negative. It goes deeper into the back story of Wonka which helps humanize him but can also take away from the allure of his mystery. Also, I personally don't feel like Danny Elfman's music really stands out in this one. It doesn't help that, for most people, this one has to fight a constant comparison to the original. 

This really just highlights some of the differences. I would say that the original is better but that doesn't mean the 2005 film is bad especially when taking into account the challenge of reinterpreting an already adapted story in a new way
